kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
locale: en
buttonLabel: "Discover nature in Bolivia, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Bolivia, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay feature in an extensive 32-day journey through eight countries with both Nature and Wildlife and Safari themes. Yet the itinerary does not include four separate wildlife-watching programmes in these four countries. Bolivia offers highland lagoons, Peru Lake Titicaca and the Andes, Colombia an outing to Guatapé Rock, and Uruguay a city tour. The main island-based nature experience of the full journey is in Ecuador, on the Galápagos.
---

## Wildlife and safari: what is actually included in the selected countries?

Our [Bolivia, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay combination](/multi-country/bolivia_colombia_peru_uruguay/) under the Wildlife and Safari theme features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The current selection is formed by the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), whose Wildlife and Safari theme applies to the **trip as a whole**, thanks to the included observations on the Galápagos.

The four named countries are only part of this longer route: Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Ecuador also feature in the main programme. A thematic label must therefore not be read as a promise of wildlife watching in every one of the four countries.

The practical question on this page is **which specific nature stages belong to the selected geography, and where the most substantial wildlife experiences are found on the full itinerary**.

## Bolivia: lagoons, highlands and geothermal scenery

The Bolivia stage begins after Chile's Atacama Desert. A two-day 4×4 route passes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the Dalí Desert, geothermal areas, Laguna Colorada and a chain of other lagoons before reaching [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Of the selected four countries, this is the richest stage in terms of varied natural landscapes.

Bolivia's high-altitude lakes have their own birdlife, but the confirmed programme **does not allocate a separate guaranteed excursion to observe particular bird species**. It is described as a 4×4 tour between geographical sites. Landscapes, salt flats and geothermal phenomena are its advertised attractions; encountering animals is a possibility, not a fixed outcome.

Another key consideration is elevation above 4,000 m. Weather protection, sun exposure and altitude tolerance matter more here than a wish list of species.

## Peru: the Andes and Titicaca, not a specialist safari

In [Peru](/peru/), the trip begins at [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). Travellers then cross the Andes to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Lima.

The lake ecosystem and high-altitude species are fascinating in their own right. However, the published Peru days primarily feature cultural and sightseeing excursions, a coach, trains and archaeological monuments. The programme does not include a dedicated wildlife-tracking trek or an expedition into the Peruvian Amazon.

If Peru's fauna is your priority, choose from the [catalogue of wildlife-watching trips through Peru](/interests/wildlife/tours/peru/) and review the individual days rather than assuming the nature specialisation of one itinerary applies to every other product.

## Colombia: landscapes and cities without a promised wildlife expedition

The Colombia section includes [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and El Peñón Rock, followed by [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/). The included programme focuses on city excursions, viewpoints and historical sights.

Colombia has diverse natural regions, yet **this particular 32-day route does not include a standalone Amazon rainforest wildlife excursion or a specialist ornithological tour in Colombia**. Only the actual listed destinations and outings should be promised for this stage.

The choice is whether scenery accompanying a cultural itinerary is enough, or whether you want a separate themed expedition in Colombia. In the latter case, look at [Colombia nature tours](/interests/nature/tours/colombia/) instead of expecting an informal extension of the Guatapé excursion.

## Uruguay: Montevideo as a city day

In [Uruguay](/uruguay/), the itinerary includes a one-day ferry trip from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) with a sightseeing tour. This is a historical and urban part of the journey.

It **does not include marine mammal watching or a separate visit to a reserve**. Simply crossing the Río de la Plata estuary by ferry does not turn the day into a nature safari. Uruguay expands the tour's geography but does not increase the number of confirmed wildlife excursions.

## Where the full tour's main wildlife experiences take place

An important nature stage occurs **outside the selected four countries**. After Peru, the programme moves to Ecuador, where the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) are on the itinerary. Santa Cruz has nature excursions, while the marine day includes **one of two alternatives**: North Seymour with Bachas or South Plaza with Cape Carrión. Both options are not advertised as simultaneous visits.

The Galápagos section is what gives the extensive tour its pronounced wildlife component. On the Brazil stage, a visit to the Iguazu Bird Park is possible at an additional charge. These are in other countries, not Bolivia, Colombia, Peru or Uruguay.

For travellers primarily interested in animals, compare [Ecuador and Galápagos itineraries](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/) with the complete eight-country tour. The longer trip offers more geography and culture but less time for specialised observation in every region.

## What to consider when choosing a trip

First decide whether you want particular animal species, walks through natural areas or simply varied scenery. Then review each tour day: is wildlife observation described as a separate excursion, which stage is part of the main programme, where is there an alternative route, and which activities require additional payment?

Ada Tours can help align nature stops with the wider logistics: Bolivia's altitude, distances between cities, flights and days by the sea. Encounters with wild animals cannot be guaranteed even on specialised itineraries.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in the four countries

### Does each country include a separate wildlife-watching excursion?

No. Uruguay is a city day, Colombia primarily offers urban excursions, and Peru focuses on cultural sites and Titicaca. Bolivia offers highland lagoons, but a dedicated excursion to observe particular species is not guaranteed.

### Why does the tour appear under Wildlife and Safari?

Because the theme describes the complete 32-day journey through eight countries. In particular, Ecuador has a Galápagos nature programme. The thematic filter does not distribute the same interest equally across all countries.

### Can I visit both alternative Galápagos island routes?

The current programme includes one of two options, selected during confirmation. Alternative routes should not be counted as two guaranteed excursions.

### How can I find a trip with more emphasis on wildlife?

Compare the [complete wildlife-watching tour catalogue](/interests/wildlife/tours/) and itineraries for individual countries. Focus on the excursions actually offered and their duration.

kind: multi_country_combination
status: approved
locale: en
buttonLabel: "Explore journeys through Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay reveal three very different sides of South America: high-altitude lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat, the Colombian Andes and Caribbean coast, and Montevideo's European-influenced districts beside the Río de la Plata. On our current itinerary, Uruguay is visited for just one day by ferry from Buenos Aires; Bolivia comes later via Chile, and Colombia completes the eight-country journey. The main considerations are re-entry into Argentina, long transfers, different currencies and climates, and sensible allocation of time.
---

## Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay: three countries you cannot link by one short overland journey

The most unexpected destination in this combination is [Uruguay](/uruguay/). Its capital [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) lies across the Río de la Plata estuary from Buenos Aires. [Bolivia](/bolivia/) evokes the high Andes and [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). [Colombia](/colombia/) is in northern South America; the tour visits [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/).

The combination appeals to travellers interested in the contrast between a port city, Andean nature and Colombian history. But huge distances and other countries lie between these destinations. **Our selection includes tours in which all three are main-route countries, not trips limited exclusively to those three.**

Our current catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The published [“8 South American Countries in 32 Days” tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) starts in Brazil and Argentina, includes a day in Uruguay, then visits Chile and Bolivia, followed by Peru and Ecuador, and ends in Colombia. A trip confined to Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay would require separate planning of flights, duration and excursions.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

| Route section | Defining feature |
|---|---|
| Uruguay | Montevideo in one day |
| Bolivia | 4×4 vehicles, lagoons and Uyuni |
| Colombia | Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá |

## Uruguay: crossing the Río de la Plata and returning to Argentina

The Uruguay day on the current itinerary starts early in **Buenos Aires**. Travellers transfer to the port and take the ferry to Montevideo. An English-speaking guide leads the excursion, followed by free time and the return ferry to Buenos Aires. **There is no overnight stay in Uruguay on this itinerary; ferry tickets are included.**

The [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) excursion covers the port, Independence Square, the Old Town and cathedral. Compared with Bolivia's mountain stages, it is a compact city stop: the purpose is to explore the capital across the Río de la Plata, not to travel in depth along the Uruguayan coastline.

The chief logistical issue is **two international border crossings on the same day and re-entry into Argentina**. Ferry tickets do not remove the need to check passports and eligibility for entry and re-entry according to each traveller's nationality. If a visa is required, whether it is single- or multiple-entry may matter. Departure port, check-in time, the return service and its connection with the following day's itinerary also need coordination.

A standalone Uruguay trip could include other cities and the coast, but that would be a different programme. The eight-country tour has a specific objective here: an introduction to Montevideo in one sightseeing day.

## Bolivia: an extended high-altitude stage, not a city stop

Bolivia involves much more substantial travel through natural landscapes. After San Pedro de Atacama in Chile, travellers cross the land border and journey by 4×4 through high-altitude lagoons and volcanic scenery. The itinerary includes [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), the [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) area and [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/).

**These days cannot be swapped with the Montevideo visit without rebuilding the entire transport itinerary.** Uruguay appears early in the longer journey; Bolivia follows Chile. Adding both to a shorter trip would require determining flights between the regions, a suitable entry point into Bolivia and overnight stays before high-altitude excursions.

The Bolivia stage carries another risk: rapid altitude gain. The eight-country programme includes an adaptation stop in San Pedro de Atacama before the border crossing, but individual reactions vary. Headaches, nausea and pronounced tiredness can occur at altitude; being comfortable on city walks is no guarantee of feeling well here. Pace, the need for medical advice and additional acclimatisation days should be discussed in advance.

Cold, windy mountain nights and exposed lagoons require suitable layers, while solar radiation remains strong even in cool weather. A journey covering Bolivia after Uruguay needs clothing for both a coastal city and an off-road highland route.

## Colombia: several climate zones within one country

The Colombia stage of the current itinerary begins **after Ecuador**. Travellers arrive in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), head to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and explore Comuna 13. They then fly to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) on the Caribbean coast and later to [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) for an excursion to the Salt Cathedral in [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/).

This ending changes the journey's atmosphere: after Bolivia's dry, cold highlands, travellers arrive in green mountain valleys, head towards the sea and then reach another high-altitude city. Cartagena is generally hot and humid; Bogotá is noticeably cooler. Pack for a hot coastline and cool mountain evenings.

Replacing Colombia with a brief flight connection would remove a substantial part of the itinerary: Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá all have their own sightseeing days. When shortening a longer trip, decide which Colombian stops are essential before looking for flights.

## Five practical checks before booking

1. **Montevideo and Buenos Aires.** Check both border crossings during the day, documents for Uruguay and re-entry conditions for Argentina. Confirm ferry check-in and time after the tour.
2. **Long-distance connections.** Identify which countries remain between Uruguay, Bolivia and Colombia. The published itinerary visits Chile, Peru and Ecuador along the way; a shorter version does not automatically inherit its flights.
3. **Altitude and wellbeing.** Allow time to adapt before Bolivia's lagoons and to rest. A 4×4 journey to Uyuni differs substantially from sightseeing in Montevideo.
4. **Payments.** Uruguay uses the Uruguayan peso, Bolivia the boliviano and Colombia the Colombian peso. The ferry day also requires planning for expenses in Argentina, where the Argentine peso is used. Check the ability to use your particular card abroad with your bank and arrange backup payment methods.
5. **Baggage and health.** Warm layers will be useful in the Andes, lightweight clothing in Cartagena. Check flight baggage rules and health requirements in countries of entry and transit for the actual itinerary. Discuss vaccinations and medical contraindications with a qualified doctor.

Colombia offers the online Check-Mig service for submitting travel details in advance. Its immigration authority says the service is voluntary and free; passport and visa requirements still need to be checked separately. For Uruguay and Argentina, be sure to check **the outward and return journey**, not just permission for first entry.

We help coordinate the sequence of transfers, document requirements based on nationality, overnight stays and the actual programme. Confirmed terms depend on the selected tour; any separate change of itinerary requires a new quotation.

## When this particular combination makes sense

Uruguay, Bolivia and Colombia suit travellers who want to see very different aspects of South America in one trip: Montevideo on the Río de la Plata, the highlands and the cities of Colombia's Andes and Caribbean coast. **Uruguay remains a short urban episode**, while Bolivia and Colombia require substantially more time.

For comparison, explore [Uruguay tours](/uruguay/tour/), [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/) and [Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/). If [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) or [historic Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) is your main interest, a trip can be built around one of these destinations, with the others added only when enough time is available.

## Frequently asked questions about Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay

### Is an overnight stay in Montevideo included?

No. The published [Montevideo day trip](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) starts and ends in Buenos Aires on the same day. The return ferry and hotel transfer are part of that day's programme.

### Do travellers have to re-enter Argentina after Uruguay?

Yes. On this itinerary, travellers return from Uruguay to Argentina. Specific visa, permitted-entry and document rules depend on nationality and must be checked in advance.

### Why are Bolivia and Colombia separated by several countries?

Because the current product is an extensive tourist itinerary through eight countries, not a standalone three-country tour. After Bolivia, it passes through Peru and Ecuador before reaching Colombia.

### Can the published price be used for a short tour of the three countries?

No. The price applies to the complete [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) with its specific excursions, accommodation and flights. Different geography and duration require a new calculation.

locale: en
buttonLabel: "Explore adventures in Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  On a wider South American journey, Bolivia offers two days of high-altitude 4×4 travel, Colombia an excursion to El Peñón Rock and the Guatapé reservoir, and Uruguay a one-day ferry trip to Montevideo. These stages have different physical demands and purposes. We explain why the Adventure theme does not mean a sporting programme in every country, how the stops are distributed in time and what to prepare for the transfers.
---

## Three countries, three very different travel days

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. It is currently based on the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), where Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay appear together **in the filter**, but are far apart in the actual itinerary. The tour also visits Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Peru and Ecuador. This page does not promise a ready-made sporting trip limited to the selected three countries.

The most adventurous section is the Bolivian highlands, featuring 4×4 vehicles, lagoons and the Uyuni Salt Flat. In Colombia, an excursion from Medellín takes travellers to the rock and town of Guatapé, with views across the reservoir. Uruguay is different: travellers take a ferry from Buenos Aires to Montevideo, explore the city and return to Argentina. **Extreme sports, trekking and off-road touring are not included in Uruguay**.

For options without the adventure theme, see [all tours featuring Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay](/multi-country/bolivia_colombia_uruguay/). For other country combinations focused on active experiences, browse [multi-country adventure travel](/multi-country/interests/adventure/).

## Uruguay: ferry and Montevideo early in the longer journey

Day nine includes an early transfer to the port of Buenos Aires, a ferry across the Río de la Plata, a meeting with an English-speaking guide and a sightseeing excursion in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). Stops include the [port](/uruguay/place/montevideo-port/), [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/), [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) and [cathedral](/uruguay/place/montevideo-cathedral/). After free time, travellers return by ferry and transfer to their hotel in Buenos Aires. **Ferry tickets are included in the current programme.**

This is a busy international sightseeing day, where the main challenges are the early start, schedules and border formalities rather than physical effort. It offers the chance to visit another country without changing hotels overnight. Since the return journey crosses the border again, documents and entry rules must be checked against nationality, number of entries and travel date. Permission for a single entry cannot automatically be assumed to cover every crossing.

The sequence matters: **Montevideo comes before Bolivia and Colombia**, not between them. Travellers first return to Buenos Aires, then fly to Chile and only later cross Atacama into highland Bolivia. Uruguay is not a direct transport link to Bolivia.

For a cultural introduction rather than a sporting route, explore the [Montevideo excursion](/uruguay/montevideo/montevideo-day-trip-from-buenos-aires/). A separate adventure in Uruguay would call for a different itinerary with confirmed activities.

## Bolivia: the principal high-altitude adventure

Bolivia follows San Pedro de Atacama and a border crossing from Chile. The included [two-day 4×4 itinerary](/bolivia/uyuni/uyuni-salt-flats-4x4-tour-2-days/) has an English-speaking guide and visits Laguna Verde, the Dalí Desert, Polques springs, Sol de Mañana and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The next day features other high-altitude lagoons, views of Ollagüe Volcano, Chiguana Salt Flat and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). At the salt flat, stops include Colchani, the “Eyes of Water” and an island with cacti.

Here travellers face remote landscapes, long drives and elevations above 4,000 m. Conditions can be challenging without extended hiking: the tour explicitly mentions altitude sickness as a risk. Accommodation is in an expedition-style hotel. Appropriate clothing, water, sun protection and altitude tolerance must be considered before travel.

The included format is a **guided 4×4 journey**, not driving an off-road vehicle yourself or taking part in a rally. Departure times and stops follow the itinerary, so opportunities to take photographs depend on the schedule, weather and safe road conditions. For more options, see [Bolivia adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/bolivia/).

Afterwards, the group flies from Uyuni to La Paz and continues via Tiwanaku into Peru. The itinerary does not return to Uruguay's sea-level climate immediately after the highland days; travel remains in the Andes for some time.

## Colombia: El Peñón and Guatapé after crossing the Andes

Colombia comes considerably later than Uruguay and Bolivia. Between them lie the Peru section, Quito and the Galápagos, followed by a flight via Guayaquil to [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). The actual Bolivia-to-Colombia journey therefore includes other countries and flights.

From Medellín, travellers join the [El Peñón and Guatapé excursion](/colombia/medellin/el-penol-guatape-from-medellin/). The itinerary names a replica of old El Peñol, [El Peñón de Guatapé Rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/), the colourful facades of [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and reservoir views. The excursion lasts about eight hours and includes an English-speaking guide.

**Visiting the rock does not automatically mean the climb to its summit is included.** Whether the stairs are part of the specific excursion version, access and conditions must be confirmed separately. The larger tour continues through Comuna 13, Cartagena, Bogotá and the Zipaquirá Salt Cathedral. Those are primarily cultural sightseeing days, not a continuous adventure marathon.

Other options are available among [Colombia adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/colombia/), but check the contents of each itinerary: the active part of a broad multi-country trip may be concentrated in another country.

## Physical demands in the actual sequence

| Country | Main challenge |
|---|---|
| Uruguay | Ferry and early start |
| Bolivia | Altitude and two 4×4 days |
| Colombia | A day at the rock and town |

The contrast in climates and travel formats is pronounced. Uruguay's excursion from Buenos Aires starts at the port and continues with city walks. Bolivia calls for warm highland clothing, sun protection and preparation for road conditions. Colombia rounds out the trip with mountainous Medellín, warm Cartagena and Bogotá. Pack for the complete eight-country journey rather than only the three countries named in the filter.

Documents and payments also require separate consideration: Uruguay is visited with a return to Argentina, Bolivia follows Chile, and Colombia follows Ecuador. Entry rules, transit requirements, payment restrictions and medical conditions may differ by country and nationality. Ada Tours helps arrange the order of flights, the ferry day, road transfers and excursions. Additional active activities or a shorter journey would be a new programme with its own quotation.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay

### Are there active adventures in Uruguay on this tour?

Uruguay is represented by a [one-day Montevideo trip](/uruguay/montevideo/montevideo-day-trip-from-buenos-aires/): ferry, sightseeing and return to Buenos Aires. No sporting activities are listed for that day.

### Are Montevideo ferry tickets included?

Yes. Ferry tickets are included in the [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Transfer arrangements, departure times and documents are checked for the agreed travel dates.

### Will I need to drive a 4×4 vehicle in Bolivia?

No. The tour describes a two-day guided 4×4 route with an English-speaking guide. The main challenges are the high-altitude environment and long drives.

### Can I visit just these three countries?

A custom itinerary can be designed. The existing tour, however, covers eight countries, with Uruguay, Bolivia and Colombia in different sections. A shortened version requires reworking logistics, visits and price.

buttonLabel: "Explore the history of Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay reveal three distinct chapters of South American history: pre-Columbian Tiwanaku in the Andean highlands, Colombia's historical districts and urban culture, and port-city Montevideo beside the Río de la Plata. On the current Ada Tours itinerary, the countries belong to an extensive 32-day journey through eight nations. Here we examine which cultural visits are included and how much time is actually allocated to them.
---

## What connects a cultural journey through Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay?

One trip can reveal very different periods of the continent's history. [Bolivia](/bolivia/) introduces Tiwanaku civilisation and highland urban traditions. [Uruguay](/uruguay/) adds Montevideo's port heritage and architecture on the shores of the Río de la Plata. [Colombia](/colombia/) continues the story through Medellín's neighbourhoods, colonial Cartagena and Bogotá's museums.

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} combining these countries with a culture and history theme. The main offering is currently [“8 South American Countries in 32 Days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). This **visits eight main-route countries**, also including Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Peru and Ecuador. The three-country filter identifies an itinerary matching the selected geography; it does not imply a standalone tour of just Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay.

| Country | Cultural focus |
|---|---|
| Bolivia | La Paz and Tiwanaku archaeology |
| Uruguay | Historic Montevideo in one day |
| Colombia | Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá |

## Bolivia: Tiwanaku and the living city of La Paz

After the high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni Salt Flat, the journey continues in [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). The city excursion introduces neighbourhoods, local markets and contrasting buildings on steep slopes. The following day, the route leads to [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) and onward towards the Peruvian border.

Tiwanaku is a distinct ancient Andean civilisation. Its political and religious centre flourished long before the rise of the Inca state. The archaeological complex is notable for stone structures, ceremonial spaces and the famous Gate of the Sun. The site is UNESCO World Heritage and one of the most substantial historical experiences on the Bolivia stage.

The difference between a city tour and an archaeological outing is especially apparent here. In La Paz, you encounter the contemporary life of a highland capital; in Tiwanaku, the material traces of a culture that cannot be reduced to later Inca history. The site is visited **on the road from Bolivia into Peru**, so the day also involves an overland journey and a border crossing. There is no extra free day for archaeological exploration in the programme.

## Uruguay: a single Montevideo day on the long journey

Uruguay is organised differently. On day nine, travellers take the ferry from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), join a guided city excursion in English, enjoy some free time and return. It is a good introduction to the capital, **not a multi-day exploration of Uruguay**.

In the historic part of the city, the tour highlights Independence Square, old streets and the cathedral. Montevideo developed as a port and administrative centre beside the Río de la Plata; its streetscape makes an interesting comparison with Buenos Aires, where the day begins. For a one-day visit, ferry times and the return journey matter more than trying to add several distant sights.

A deeper look at Uruguay's cities, wineries or Atlantic coast would require changing the itinerary. The included Montevideo trip gives no basis for promising excursions to other parts of the country.

## Colombia: from Comuna 13 to colonial Cartagena

The Colombia section comes towards the end of the route and offers a more diverse urban programme. In [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), travellers explore Comuna 13 and visit El Peñón and Guatapé. The next stage is [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), where the old city reflects the history of Caribbean maritime trade and Spanish colonial fortifications.

Cartagena's colonial fortifications are UNESCO World Heritage. After highland La Paz and the more intimate scale of Montevideo, Cartagena offers a different urban experience: a warm Caribbean shoreline, narrow streets and the defensive architecture of a port. These substantial differences between countries make a multi-stage route worthwhile.

The final section includes Bogotá. Stops include the historic La Candelaria district, the Gold Museum, the Mint Museum, the Botero Collection and the Monserrate viewpoint. A separate excursion visits the Salt Cathedral at Zipaquirá. Opening days matter: **the Gold Museum is closed on Mondays, while the Mint Museum and Botero Collection close on Tuesdays**. The sightseeing order must account for these closures.

## Why country order matters in a cultural itinerary

These three countries **do not follow one another** on the existing tour. Montevideo is visited from Argentina early in the journey; Bolivia follows Chile and precedes Peru; Colombia concludes the programme after Ecuador and the Galápagos. The three countries cannot simply be extracted from the longer route with the same excursions intact without recalculating flights and overland transfers.

When discussing a custom version, Ada Tours helps identify which experiences matter most: a day in port-city Montevideo, more time for Andean culture, or a series of Colombian city visits. Flights, sightseeing days and guiding are then arranged. That approach is more valuable than automatically adding another city to an itinerary already full of transfers.

For a cultural trip focused solely on Bolivia, explore the country's [history-focused tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/bolivia/). For broader choices across the continent, see [multi-country cultural and historical routes](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/). The [general Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay selection](/multi-country/bolivia_colombia_uruguay/) features other thematic emphases.

## Practical issues: altitude, excursions and documents

Altitude is the main physical consideration on Bolivia's cultural stage. Tiwanaku sits at roughly 3,850 m, and the itinerary reaches it after several days in the Andes. Even when visiting monuments without an athletic hike, travellers need acclimatisation time, water, sun protection and attention to their wellbeing. The programme includes an acclimatisation stop in San Pedro de Atacama before Bolivia's highlands.

Uruguay involves different demands: an early ferry departure, a city tour and returning on the same day. In Colombia, important factors are urban transfers, flights, museum schedules and the progression from Medellín through Cartagena to Bogotá. Ada Tours coordinates the order of visits and confirms current conditions for each excursion when planning a journey.

Documents for multiple border crossings are checked **according to the traveller's nationality**, including entry, transit and return connections. Payments also need planning in bolivianos, Colombian pesos and Uruguayan pesos, along with bank-card and cash availability. No single entry authorisation or universally accepted bank card can be assumed for these countries.

## Frequently asked questions about a cultural trip through Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay

### Is there a ready-made tour visiting only these three countries?

The selection features the longer [eight-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay are main-route countries but separated by other stages. A trip limited to these three countries must be planned separately.

### How much time is spent in Montevideo?

The itinerary allocates one day to a ferry excursion from Buenos Aires, a city tour and the return journey. No additional overnight stays in Uruguay are included.

### Is Tiwanaku included?

Yes, [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) is visited on the day of travel from La Paz towards the Peruvian border. It is a significant archaeological stop within a busy transport day.

### What would appeal most to history lovers in Colombia?

The route combines [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and its fortifications and historic streets with Bogotá's museums and colonial centre. Medellín adds modern urban history and an introduction to Comuna 13.

### Can Bogotá's museums be scheduled on any day?

No. The Gold Museum, Mint Museum and Botero Collection have different closing days. Their schedules must be considered when planning the excursion without dropping required programme elements.

## What the Nature theme means for Bolivia, Colombia and Uruguay

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} for these countries — [“8 South American Countries in 32 Days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Eight countries form one journey: **the three-country thematic filter does not remove the remaining five countries from the itinerary or price**.

In terms of nature, each selected country serves a different purpose. Bolivia is the major highland landscape stage. Colombia offers a day beside a monolith and reservoir. Uruguay is a short city tour reached by ferry from Argentina. Understanding these differences helps travellers decide whether this programme suits a primarily nature-focused trip.

## Uruguay: Montevideo is a city excursion, not a nature expedition

Uruguay appears in the itinerary shortly after Buenos Aires in Argentina. A day trip to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) includes an early port transfer, a ferry crossing, sightseeing with an English-speaking guide and the return to Buenos Aires after some free time.

The route introduces the port, historic urban environment and national capital. The Río de la Plata estuary forms the setting for the crossing, but the confirmed day's programme **includes no separate nature reserve, national park, safari or beach holiday in Uruguay**. It would be a mistake to expect the same nature experiences from this stop as from Bolivia.

If Uruguay's own natural areas are the priority, a standard city-excursion day is insufficient. A different itinerary with more stops and time would be needed, without automatically promising particular parks or Ada Tours services.

## Bolivia: the richest nature days in this combination

After Argentina, Uruguay and Chile, the eight-country itinerary enters the Bolivian highlands. From San Pedro de Atacama, a two-day guided 4×4 journey passes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), the Salvador Dalí Desert, thermal springs and the Sol de Mañana geothermal area on the way to [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/).

The following day takes in more high-altitude lagoons, the Ollagüe Volcano area, Chiguana Salt Flat and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The colours of the lakes, textures of the rock formations and surfaces of the salt flats change along the route. The Los Lípez region also has important high-altitude wetlands, but the confirmed tourist format is a **guided 4×4 journey**, not a separate excursion to seek rare birds.

The group then flies to La Paz and visits its surroundings, including Moon Valley. Given the altitude, remote stops and long transfers, Bolivia's days should be assessed against the actual itinerary and individual wellbeing, rather than just the number of lagoons listed.

## Colombia: a day at Guatapé within a city-focused section

Colombia appears near the end of the trip, after Peru and Ecuador. From [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), the itinerary visits [El Peñón de Guatapé Rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). Travellers explore the settlement, monolith and views of a large artificial reservoir.

This guided excursion in English takes approximately eight hours. Visiting the rock area is listed, but a ticket to climb to the top must not automatically be assumed to be included. Subsequent days focus on Cartagena, Bogotá and Colombia's historical attractions.

Thus, “Nature and Colombia” here means **a specific scenic experience at Guatapé**, not a promised multi-day humid-forest expedition or wildlife safari.

| Uruguay | One day in Montevideo by ferry |
